Born David Robert Jones in London, he reached an international audience as Ziggy Stardust and later with Let's Dance. long_biography.plain_text:
Musician David Bowie's art collection grew through detailed study of the painters whose work interested him. Working with adviser Kate Chertavian, he studied Modern British painters, visited artists and lived among the pictures he bought. He readily lent works to exhibitions, including Frank Auerbach's portrait of Gerda Boehm for a Royal Academy retrospective.

BowieNet brought his audience into an online community. Launched with UltraStar in 1998, the internet service let subscribers build personal web pages, join live chats and explore exclusive material. A songwriting competition invited fans to complete verses for What's Really Happening, offering the winner a publishing contract and the opportunity to attend its recording.

uncertainties: Research date 1 October 2026; wealth and relationship are assessed immediately before death in January 2016. Posthumous estate licences and disposal demonstrate retained rights but are not personal current holdings.

Music is a reasoned principal-core conclusion supported by personally monetised rights and enduring catalogue control, without a complete terminal balance sheet. Art ownership is substantive but does not by itself establish a competing fortune-creation sector.

Broad Self-made deliberately leaves original launch advantages unresolved. Founder describes creation of the owned music platform under the permitted contract, not a claim that every record label or collaborator belonged to him.

Forbes-first yielded a distinct UBS adviser; musician-related articles do not constitute an authenticated personal profile. LinkedIn searches found unrelated professionals and a tribute band, so none is proposed.

Official legacy social accounts were authenticated through outbound primary links and contemporary attribution; they are not claimed to be personally operated after death. No separate company website is necessary.

Birth name is David Robert Jones, but the existing professional display name remains David Bowie. Robert is not automatically inserted into that professional-name structure; no unsupported second nationality or secondary residence is proposed.
The historical vessel end date is not independently confirmed; renamed-hull evidence resolves identity only. No vessel content enters either biography.
